new_gain.name: full-spectrum little logarithmic endpoint and spectral K-functional
new_gain.statement: For every progressive Y in L^3(Omega x (0,T);L^2(Torus)), F=||T_TY|| belongs to the strict little endpoint Z^o_{3,1}(T): lim_{s downarrow 0} s^(1/3)F^*(s)/(1+log(T/s))=0. Quantitatively, if e_N(Y) is the best L^3 approximation error by at most N dyadic spectral blocks and L=1+log(T/s), then s^(1/3)F^*(s)/L <= 947 N^(1/6)L^(-1/3)||Y||_3 + 5.2 e_N(Y), for every N>=1.
new_gain.mechanism: combine the predecessor finite-N critical Z_{3,2/3} theorem with the exact unrestricted Z_{3,1} bound through best spectral N-term approximation and the rearrangement inequality (f+g)^*(s)<=f^*(s/2)+g^*(s/2)
new_gain.source_level_change: strict full-spectrum endpoint-space refinement at the existing logarithmic exponent 1; the exponent bracket itself remains [2/3,1]
new_gain.quantitative_improvement: If e_N(Y)<=D N^{-theta}, then T_TY lies in Z_{3,alpha_theta} with alpha_theta=(4 theta+1)/(6 theta+1), and norm <=1063||Y||_3+5.2D. Any log-1 near-saturating family must have dyadic spectral complexity of order at least L^2 at quantile logarithm L, up to explicit constants.

essential_dependencies: P24 exact endpoint r_*=3 and endpoint failure
NM13-10 full critical bracket [2/3,1] and Z_{3,1} constant 1+sqrt(2)
NM13-10 finite multiband endpoint ||T_T P_S Y||_{Z_{3,2/3}} <529 N^(1/6)||P_S Y||_3 for |S|<=N
failed_or_insufficient_route: The preceding black-box multiband gluing cannot remove the N^(1/6) loss uniformly on the whole L^3 unit ball. This run instead extracts what is nevertheless uniform for every fixed input: finite-band approximants converge in the global endpoint norm, forcing a little-o logarithmic tail and yielding a best-N spectral K-functional.
residual_obstruction: Upgrade the little Z_{3,1} conclusion to a uniform Z_{3,alpha} bound with alpha<1, ideally alpha=2/3. The quantitative obstruction now says any bad family must move substantial L^3 mass through more than order L^2 dyadic bands as L grows; common-Brownian covariance/Hellinger information must rule out or realize that spectral escape.
next_attack: Apply the critical Hellinger/decoherence kernel to the best-N remainder and seek a uniform estimate on spectrally escaping families, rather than another fixed finite-band theorem.
